value.rationale: The canonical positive one-harmonic datum tests polynomial complexity in a previously studied nonlinear holomorphic Radon inversion problem. The all-harmonic/all-power-weight sharp degree threshold, rigidity and universal inverse-square-root blowup quantify a nontrivial gap from general holomorphic solvability and from ordinary Fejér–Riesz factoring. It is a natural complete finite-complexity boundary classification, not an arbitrary sample value.
